title: Basic word structure
subtitle: The small parts behind complex words.

sections.title: Roots, prefixes and suffixes
sections.read: A root carries the central idea. A prefix modifies it; a suffix often identifies a condition, function or procedure. Not every term contains all three.

sections.title: Combining forms and linking vowels
sections.read: A combining form consists of a root and combining vowel. The vowel often links roots or a root to a consonant-starting suffix. Exceptions and spelling changes need checking.

title: Public health & research
subtitle: From individuals to populations.

sections.title: Population measures and study designs
sections.read: Incidence concerns new cases in a defined population over time. Prevalence concerns existing cases at a point or over a period. Specify the population, denominator and timeframe before interpreting either measure.

sections.title: Incidence, prevalence and research vocabulary
sections.read: A cohort study follows or analyses a defined group. A case-control study compares prior exposures by outcome status, while a cross-sectional study measures a population at a particular time. Study designs answer different questions.

terms.definition: The occurrence of new cases in a population at risk over a specified period.
terms.plain: How many new cases develop over time.
terms.example: The study reports incidence over a defined follow-up period.
terms.note: A rate and a cumulative incidence use different denominators; always read the study’s definition.

terms.definition: The proportion of a population with a condition at a specified time or during a defined period.
terms.plain: How common a condition is in a population.
terms.example: The survey reports point prevalence on a specified date.
terms.note: Prevalence includes existing cases; incidence concerns new cases.

terms.definition: A defined group of people followed or studied over time.
terms.plain: A group whose outcomes are studied over time.
terms.example: The research follows a cohort of healthcare workers.

sections.title: Interpreting population statements accurately
sections.read: Sensitivity and specificity describe test performance conditional on disease status. Predictive values concern disease status given a test result and depend on context. Statistical significance alone does not describe the clinical size or importance of an effect.

sections.title: Clinical language, documentation and coding literacy
sections.read: Identify the documented concept first. Separate conditions, symptoms, procedures and negative findings. A word part does not establish a diagnosis or determine a code. Use the correct jurisdiction, edition, index, tabular instructions and applicable standards.
